Watts made this hymn from Psalm 72, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Endow the king with Your justice, O God, and the son of the king with Your righteousness. 2May he judge Your people with righteousness and Your afflicted with justice. 3May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills bring righteousness. 4May he vindicate the afflicted among the people; may he save the children of the needy and crush the oppressor. … 16 more verses PSALM 72 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 72
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun Does his successive journies run; His kingdom stretch from shore to shore, Till moons shall wax and wane no more. STANZA I
Watts's psalms run from Psalm 1 to Psalm 150, several settings to many psalms: 367 hymns. This is number 2. Point at a tick to see the hymn; click it to open that hymn.

Printed hymnals list, for each hymn, the Bible passages it goes with, so a church can choose a hymn for the day's reading. Gathered from the hymnals Hymnary.org catalogues, editors have tied this hymn to 43 passages in 10 books. One square is one passage; a ringed square is one the hymn's own lines echo.
